boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Carleton College
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe Northfield food destinations with currently published late hours.

cards.title: Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: 410 S Hwy 3, Northfield
cards.notes: Use the drive-through when you need a late food option; the official location page lists service through 1:00 AM daily.
cards.short_summary: A daily 1:00 AM drive-through option on Highway 3.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s Northfield location lists drive-through hours of 7:00 AM–1:00 AM every day.
cards.access_notes: Drive-through is listed open until 1:00 AM daily; dine-in hours differ.

cards.title: Carbone's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 620 S Water St, Northfield
cards.notes: Order food for dine-in, delivery, or takeout; confirm kitchen availability when arriving close to the listed 1:00 AM closing time.
cards.short_summary: Pizza, pasta, and hoagies with the latest listed closing time downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Carbone’s Northfield lists Monday–Saturday hours of 11:00 AM–1:00 AM and Sunday hours until midnight.
cards.access_notes: Listed open until 1:00 AM Monday–Saturday and midnight Sunday; food offerings are listed on the location page.

cards.title: Applebee's Grill + Bar
cards.subtitle: 2433 Hwy 3 S, Northfield
cards.notes: Use dine-in, pickup, delivery, or Carside To Go for food; its location page publishes midnight restaurant hours every day.
cards.short_summary: A highway restaurant with daily midnight hours and multiple food-ordering options.
cards.evidence_claim: Applebee’s Northfield lists restaurant hours of 11:00 AM–12:00 AM Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant hours are listed until midnight daily; use food ordering rather than bar service.

cards.title: McDonald's
cards.subtitle: 1101 S Hwy 3, Northfield
cards.notes: Check the official location page before leaving; it lists restaurant and drive-through service until 11:00 PM most nights.
cards.short_summary: A South Highway 3 food stop with published 11:00 PM service.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald’s at 1101 S Hwy 3 lists lobby hours until 11:00 PM daily, with Friday and Saturday drive-through service until 11:30 PM.
cards.access_notes: Lobby closes at 11:00 PM daily; Friday and Saturday drive-through closes at 11:30 PM.

cards.title: Culver's
cards.subtitle: 960 Hwy 3 S, Northfield
cards.notes: Plan for dine-in by 10:00 PM, or use the later drive-through window Wednesday through Saturday when it is listed open to 11:00 PM.
cards.short_summary: A drive-through option with later midweek-to-weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Culver’s Northfield lists dine-in hours until 10:00 PM daily and drive-through hours until 11:00 PM Wednesday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Culver's of Northfield, MN — Hwy 3 S
cards.access_notes: Dine-in closes at 10:00 PM daily; drive-through is listed until 11:00 PM Wednesday–Saturday.

cards.title: El Tequila
cards.subtitle: 1010 MN-3 S, Northfield
cards.notes: Choose the restaurant’s food service for a later dinner; the official Northfield page lists daily hours ending at 10:00 PM.
cards.short_summary: A Mexican restaurant on Minnesota 3 with daily 10:00 PM hours.
cards.evidence_claim: El Tequila’s Northfield location lists hours of 11:00 AM–10:00 PM Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: The official Northfield page lists food-service hours until 10:00 PM every day.

cards.title: Pizza Hut
cards.subtitle: 1500 Clinton Ln, Northfield
cards.notes: Use delivery or carryout for a Friday or Saturday food pickup; the official store page lists those services until 10:00 PM.
cards.short_summary: A Clinton Lane delivery and carryout option with 10:00 PM weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut at 1500 Clinton Lane lists delivery and carryout hours until 10:00 PM Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Delivery and carryout are listed until 10:00 PM Friday and Saturday; other days end at 9:00 PM.

cards.title: Tokyo Grill
cards.subtitle: 1301 Bollenbacher Dr, Northfield
cards.notes: For a later sit-down or takeout meal, go Friday or Saturday; the restaurant’s own site lists service until 9:30 PM.
cards.short_summary: A Bollenbacher Drive restaurant open to 9:30 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Tokyo Grill lists Friday and Saturday hours of 11:00 AM–9:30 PM and identifies its Northfield address.
cards.access_notes: Listed open until 9:30 PM Friday and Saturday; Tuesday–Thursday and Sunday close at 9:00 PM.

cards.title: Taco Terco
cards.subtitle: 305 S Water St, Northfield
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s listed Water Street location for dinner; its official menu and location page shows a 9:00 PM closing time.
cards.short_summary: A Water Street restaurant with a published 9:00 PM close.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Terco’s official location page lists 305 Water Street South, Northfield and says it closes at 9:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Taco Terco menu, location, and hours
cards.access_notes: The official location section lists a 9:00 PM close; check the page for day-specific changes.

cards.title: Basil's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 301 S Water St, Northfield
cards.notes: Make this an early-evening pizza run: Carleton’s current Northfield restaurant guide lists Monday–Saturday service ending at 9:00 PM.
cards.short_summary: A long-running local pizza restaurant with published 9:00 PM weeknight and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s Northfield restaurant guide lists Basil’s Pizza at 301 Water St S, open Monday–Saturday from 5:00 PM–9:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Carleton College — Cafes, Grocery Stores, and Restaurants in Northfield
cards.access_notes: Carleton’s guide lists hours until 9:00 PM Monday through Saturday; Basil’s own site confirms its Northfield location.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time around Carleton, with access limits noted.

cards.title: Hike the Cowling Arboretum trails
cards.subtitle: Cowling Arboretum, adjacent to campus
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a trail walk and stay on marked routes; check the visitor rules before heading into either section of the Arb.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission walk through Carleton’s roughly 800-acre Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton states that the Cowling Arboretum is open to public use year-round and has an extensive trail system.
cards.access_notes: Open to public use year-round; follow Arboretum visitor rules.

cards.title: Run the Arb trail system
cards.subtitle: Cowling Arboretum, adjacent to campus
cards.notes: Use the trail map to choose a comfortable loop, yield thoughtfully, and keep the outing social by setting a regroup point before starting.
cards.short_summary: A trail-running hang on the Arb’s public-use paths.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton identifies the Arboretum as year-round public-use land and describes its trail system as suitable for running.
cards.access_notes: Open to public use year-round; use designated trails.

cards.title: Ride designated Upper Arb trails
cards.subtitle: Upper Cowling Arboretum, south of Highway 19
cards.notes: Bring a bike and follow the map’s designated routes only; the visitor rules prohibit cycling in the Lower Arboretum.
cards.short_summary: A bring-your-own-bike outing on the Arb’s permitted Upper Arb routes.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s Arboretum trail map says visitors enjoy limited biking and permits bikes only on specifically designated Upper Arboretum trails.
cards.source_title: Cowling Arboretum Trail Map and Rules for Visitors
cards.access_notes: Bring your own bike; cycling is allowed only on designated Upper Arb trails.

cards.title: Take a Lower Arb nature walk
cards.subtitle: Lower Cowling Arboretum, north of Highway 19
cards.notes: Walk the lower trails for a quieter nature-focused outing, keeping to the route and respecting seasonal deer-hunt restrictions.
cards.short_summary: A public trail walk through the Arb’s lower, floodplain section.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s visitor map welcomes visitors, describes Lower Arb trails and states that public use during the deer archery hunt is restricted to trails.
cards.source_title: Cowling Arboretum Trail Map and Rules for Visitors
cards.access_notes: Use trails only; during the deer archery hunt, public use is restricted to trails.

cards.title: See a Weitz Center exhibit
cards.subtitle: Weitz Center for Creativity, Carleton campus
cards.notes: Check the current arts calendar, then meet in the building’s exhibition areas and take time to compare what each person notices.
cards.short_summary: An exhibit-focused visit in Carleton’s arts center.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton states that most exhibits at the Weitz Center are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Most exhibits are free and open to the public; confirm the individual listing before visiting.

cards.title: Catch a free Weitz performance
cards.subtitle: Weitz Center for Creativity, Carleton campus
cards.notes: Choose a listed performance with free admission, arrive a little early, and use the lobby as a low-key pre-show meetup spot.
cards.short_summary: A performance outing in Carleton’s arts center when the listed show is free.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton states that most performances in Weitz Center spaces are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Most performances are free and open to the public; verify admission on the specific event listing.

cards.title: Go to a free Weitz film screening
cards.subtitle: Weitz Center for Creativity, Carleton campus
cards.notes: Find a screening marked free on the arts calendar and make it a shared movie night without needing to buy a ticket.
cards.short_summary: A cinema outing at Weitz when the screening is listed as free.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton states that most movie screenings in Weitz Center spaces are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Most movie screenings are free and open to the public; verify the individual screening’s admission details.

cards.title: Attend a Carleton Convocation
cards.subtitle: Carleton College Chapel
cards.notes: Look for the next speaker on the college calendar and invite a classmate to discuss one idea from the talk after it ends.
cards.short_summary: A speaker event presented at Carleton’s Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus-tour material describes Convocation as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public according to Carleton’s tour material; confirm the current schedule and venue.

cards.entity_name: Carleton student theater and dance performances
cards.title: See a student performance
cards.subtitle: Weitz Center for Creativity, Carleton campus
cards.notes: Check the performance calendar for a student-produced theater or dance show, then plan around the listed venue and start time.
cards.short_summary: A no-ticket student arts outing when the show is listed as free.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus-tour material says student theater and dance performances occur regularly and are free.
cards.access_notes: Consult the current arts calendar for a scheduled student performance and venue details.

cards.entity_name: Carleton Association of Nature and Outdoor Enthusiasts equipment lending
cards.title: Borrow outdoor gear through CANOE
cards.subtitle: Carleton College, Northfield
cards.notes: Ask CANOE about available equipment and borrowing steps, then pair the gear with a permitted outdoor plan such as an Arb walk.
cards.short_summary: A student outdoor-gear lending option documented as free of charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s climate action plan states that CANOE lends outdoor equipment for independent student use free of charge.
cards.access_notes: For Carleton students; contact CANOE to confirm current inventory and borrowing procedures.

warnings: Several official pages establish that eligible offerings are free but do not replace checking the current event calendar, seasonal rules, or student-organization procedures before going.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Carleton College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A gentle, place-based first-weekend loop across Carleton’s campus: orient yourself, find shared spaces, and leave time for an Arb walk.

cards.title: Start at Sayles-Hill Campus Center
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · campus center
cards.notes: Use the campus center as a first landmark: locate Student Activities, mail services, the bookstore, and the Sayles-Hill Café before branching out.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for finding core campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus map lists Student Activities, Mail Services, the Bookstore, and Sayles-Hill Café in Sayles-Hill Campus Center.
cards.access_notes: Campus services and building access may vary; check current college guidance before relying on a specific office or café.

cards.title: Get your bearings on the Bald Spot
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · central quadrangle
cards.notes: Walk the open quadrangle and use the surrounding buildings to orient yourself. It is a simple reset point between the library, chapel, and academic halls.
cards.short_summary: Carleton’s central outdoor landmark for a low-key campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s facilities master plan identifies the Bald Spot as the main quadrangle, used as a gathering space and recreation area.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus area; use normal pedestrian paths and follow any posted event or grounds guidance.

cards.title: Find Gould Library before you need it
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · academic hub
cards.notes: Make a short orientation pass through the library area and note the Athenaeum. Save the exact service desk, study, and entry details for current library guidance.
cards.short_summary: A useful landmark to locate early in the weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus map lists Laurence McKinley Gould Library and identifies the Athenaeum as an event and exhibition space there.
cards.access_notes: Library entry, services, and hours can change; consult current library information before planning a visit.

cards.title: Pause by Skinner Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · campus landmark
cards.notes: Approach from the Bald Spot for a close look at the chapel’s exterior and bell tower. Treat any interior visit as event- and access-dependent.
cards.short_summary: A landmark stop beside the main quadrangle.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s chapel history describes Skinner Memorial Chapel as a campus landmark with a 108-foot bell tower.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is the reliable plan; interior access depends on college operations and scheduled events.

cards.title: Locate the Weitz Center for Creativity
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · arts venue
cards.notes: Walk to the Weitz Center and note its public-facing venues on the map, including the cinema, theater, recital hall, and teaching museum.
cards.short_summary: An arts-focused landmark with multiple mapped venues.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus map lists the Weitz Center for Creativity along with its cinema, Weitz Theater, Applebaum Recital Hall, and Perlman Teaching Museum.
cards.access_notes: Performances, exhibitions, and building access follow their own schedules; verify an event or open hours before going inside.

cards.title: Take a quiet loop past the Japanese Garden
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · outdoor area
cards.notes: Use the campus map to fold this named garden into a daylight walk, then continue toward nearby athletic and residential parts of campus.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor destination for a short daylight stroll.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus map identifies the Japanese Garden as an outdoor area on campus.
cards.access_notes: Visit in daylight and remain on established paths; landscaping work or seasonal conditions may affect access.

cards.title: Choose an Arboretum trail
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · outdoor recreation
cards.notes: Pick a trail length that matches the daylight and weather, then use the official map to stay oriented around the Upper and Lower Arboretum.
cards.short_summary: An 800-acre campus-adjacent area with mapped trails.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton describes the Cowling Arboretum as an approximately 800-acre area adjacent to campus with a 15-mile trail system and year-round public use.
cards.access_notes: Use marked trails, prepare for weather, and consult current Arboretum rules and trail conditions before setting out.

cards.title: Make Hill of Three Oaks your turnaround point
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Arboretum landmark
cards.notes: If your route reaches this named landmark, pause, confirm your position on the Arb map, and choose the return route before daylight fades.
cards.short_summary: A mapped Arboretum landmark for structuring a walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s Cowling Arboretum trail map labels Hill of Three Oaks as a landmark in the Arboretum.
cards.access_notes: Plan a daylight return, follow the trail map, and do not use this landmark as a reason to leave marked routes.

cards.title: Walk past Bell Field
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon · east campus
cards.notes: Use the eastern edge of campus as a transition back from the Arboretum. View the field from public paths and check the athletics calendar for events.
cards.short_summary: An 11-acre athletic field beside the Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton identifies Bell Field as an 11-acre site on the eastern edge of campus and home to its men’s and women’s soccer programs.
cards.access_notes: Observe from permitted areas; field availability and spectator access depend on team practices and scheduled events.

cards.title: End by locating Cowling Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · recreation landmark
cards.notes: Finish the loop by locating the recreation center and its nearby athletic facilities. Check current recreation policies before planning a workout or facility use.
cards.short_summary: A mapped recreation destination near the athletic complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Carleton’s campus map lists Cowling Recreation Center among its athletic and recreational venues.
cards.access_notes: Facility access, equipment availability, and hours are subject to current recreation-center policies.
